provenance:
PR #44 R1/R8/R13, and ADR-032 §b2a — the case that exists because the ADR kept stating a rule about image-vs-table containment that was not true. Three wordings were falsified in three review rounds; the fourth was deleted rather than rewritten, on the human's instruction. WHAT THIS CASE PINS. Containment is one comparison, `span.start <= offset < span.end`, half-open, for cells and tables alike. It has to be applied rather than predicted, because an emits nothing while a table/cell span is tightened to its first/last VISIBLE character (ADR-029 §b1) and an empty cell is clamped into the tightened table span — so the offset and the span move independently. This case applies the comparison to all nine of xom-2021's images and records the answer; ADR-032 §b2a carries the measured instances, and normalize.py::_demo pins the synthetic shapes, including the two that falsified earlier wordings (an image with its cell's text on BOTH sides, which is inside its cell with the mark strictly between start and end; and a wholly text-empty , which produces no record at all). THE CORPUS, SPLIT BY WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS. 10 of 53 sit inside
markup and 0 of 53 offsets fall inside any recorded table or cell span — but not for one reason, and saying it was "entirely" one case was wrong twice (R13). 6 of the 10 are the leading-row clamp, where a table record does exist starting 2 characters after the image: ba-2003 1 of 3, bac-2006 2 of 5, xom-2021 3 of 9. The other 4 are cvx-2015, all four of its images, whose enclosing
has no visible text anywhere in it and is dropped entirely, so no record exists near them at all — the nearest records to 133962 are (127392, 128503) and (145616, 145697). WHY xom-2021. Its cover signature block is the sharpest instance and the one ADR-032 §b2a names: g7/g8/g9 (raw bytes 2001029, 2001245, 2001461) each sit in their own
in the LEADING rows of one ; all three report normalized offset 232186 while the table is recorded at (232188, 232373) with all twelve of its empty cells clamped to 232188. The images are two characters before their own table starts. bac-2006 shows the same shape at 391006 against a table at (391008, 391112). cvx-2015 has more in-table images (4 of 4) but is NOT the sharper instance: its table is never recorded, so there is no span for the images to be outside of and the comparison has nothing to apply to. xom-2021 is also already a committed image fixture, so using it adds no corpus and no ADR-021 population movement. WHAT EACH CHECK IS FOR. The `table` check is load-bearing and not decoration: without it, `in_table: false` would also pass on an implementation that recorded no tables at all, and the assertion would be vacuous. It pins that the signature table IS recorded, with its two image-only leading rows present as all-empty rows and the officers' row derived correctly — i.e. the very table the images are claimed to be outside of. anchor "Darren W. Woods" with index 1: that string occurs in four recorded tables (records 19, 50, 123, 124 at HEAD) because the cover block is nested inside a larger layout table and repeated in the signature pages, and record 50 at (232188, 232373) is the 3-row one; index 1 selects it, per ADR-029 §c's locate rule. The nine `image` checks carry the exact offset and `in_table` for EVERY image in the filing, not just the three in-cell ones, so the six that are not in table markup pin the negative side too and a blanket `in_table` implementation cannot pass. tables_sane 110-140 bands the 126 records at HEAD. THIS CASE IS ALSO THE FIRST TO RUN tables=true AND images=true TOGETHER. Both annotations share one _Plain pass and one merged _tidy marks map (normalize.py), and until this case nothing in the suite exercised that composition on a real filing. RED FIRST (hard rule 2). Watched twice, and the first description of it was wrong -- PR #44 R9, corrected here rather than quietly replaced. What round 2 committed said: "this exact case, with in_table set to TRUE for g7/g8/g9 ... ran 3 failures", citing history line 20260824-000828 fast 81764f7 dirty 104/105 0.9905. That line was NOT this case. It carries table_cells_fidelity 0.5829 and table_rows_fidelity 0.4776, and the committed table label contributes 27 of 427 cells, which cannot drop the suite ratio below 400/427 = 0.937. The run behind it had the `table` check WITHOUT its "index": 1, so anchor "Darren W. Woods" resolved to record 19 (36 rows, 324 cells) instead of record 50, giving FOUR failures -- "grid differs: 36 rows x 9 got vs 3 x 9 labeled; cells 22/324, rows 1/36" plus the three in_table rows -- and the index was added in the same edit as the label flip. So the case as committed had never itself been watched red, and "flipping the three labels is the whole repair" was false of that run. What was then actually done, on the case EXACTLY as committed (round 3, 2026-08-24): only the three in_table values flipped to true, nothing else touched, `python3 -m evals.run --suite fast` -> [FAIL] images-in-table-cell (adversarial, 0.34s) [eval] suite 'fast': 104/105 = 0.990 [eval] table fidelity: cells 1.0000 (427/427), rows 1.0000 (34/34) image xom-20211231_g7.jpg at 232186 is outside every recorded table span, labeled in_table=True image xom-20211231_g8.jpg at 232186 is outside every recorded table span, labeled in_table=True image xom-20211231_g9.jpg at 232186 is outside every recorded table span, labeled in_table=True Three failures, and fidelity 1.0/1.0 -- which is the arithmetic that tells the two runs apart, since the misdescribed one reads 0.5829/0.4776. History line: 20260824-004456 fast 67628dd dirty 104/105 0.9905, and the red run wrote its own full report, evals/report/20260824-004456-fast.json, where the three failures can be read directly. Flipping the three labels back to false is green, 0 failures.
